title: Phones keep less of the town twice when you tap
items: Nothing you can see changed. A tap on a plank walk, a fence or the goods at a door is now answered by the graphics chip, which draws the spot under your finger once and reads back what is there.
So a phone no longer keeps a second copy of those boards and pales in page memory once they are drawn: about 16 MB less on arrival in 1835, and more as you walk.
A tap no longer opens the card of a walk or fence too far away to be drawn.
